Episode 184. Beyond Fate (2)
The final battle had begun.
Approximately five hundred ships and over six hundred dragons crisscrossed the sky of Huepester, which was dyed black.
The night upon which the existence of humanity hinged was passing by, slow and agonizing like an eternity.
Occasionally, knights and wizards on board the ships, along with demons and beastmen, found themselves enveloped in the illusion of a chill wind blowing through the ship.
Deep fear tends to manifest as a sensory experience.
The elite of each faction, having crossed numerous battles, were intensely focusing on their fighting spirit.
Even a momentary lapse could allow fear to pierce their psyche like a blade. They felt they might not be able to fight.
It wasn’t because they were inadequate. As the Tomb of Swords drew nearer, the influence of the monstrosity was growing, deepening like the night.
"A maze can exist in the sky... we should be on the right path, so why can't we spot the monster's castle?"
Vera Din spoke. Due to the thick fog of darkness that was obstructing their view, the fleet was unable to pick up speed.
The situation was the same for the reconnaissance team led by Orgal.
The true fog of darkness spread by the monstrosity rendered his Iron Gate useless.
Soon, however, Vera Din realized something.
"…We were already close."
Suddenly, as if a door was opened, the fog lifted, revealing an outrageously huge wall before their eyes.
The fog had been obscuring the castle all along.
The castle built by the monstrosity in just two days truly revealed that the reports on its size were no exaggeration, starting from the walls itself.
The hundreds of ships and dragons appeared as insignificant as mayflies before the castle.
The end of the world.
Upon seeing the monstrosity's castle, everyone could not help but have a similar thought.
This is the end of the world.
"Leader! The sky… it’s opening!"
The crimson clouds spreading above the castle were splitting in half. Descending with a force that distorted nature was a massive spaceship, a symbol of the monstrosity's power.

The shadow of 'Ram' was casting a dark shadow over the entire sky and land. Even the dragons felt flying became difficult, as if the shadow had a massive weight of its own. The wizards who were maintaining the power of the ships were breaking into a cold sweat.
In fact, the altitude was dropping. It felt as if an invisible hand was gently pressing down on the temporary alliance fleet.
No matter how hard the dragons and magicians tried, they couldn't maintain the altitude. The pressure ceased when the fleet stopped at about half the height of the walls.
"Dare we not fly over the dwelling of a god..."
In facing a god, the proper protocol is not to start the fight from a higher position.
That's how Vera Din understood the phenomenon. If they can't break through from the front, they won't be able to enter the castle.
"I anticipated that a direct attack on the castle would be impossible. Everyone, stop trying to gain altitude and calmly prepare the shields. The welcome ceremony will start soon."
At the same time, Cadun, Orgal, and Beil took their positions at the center of each formation.
This was a preparation to stop Ram's main cannon, a nightmare they experienced during the first onslaught.
Roar!
However, what suddenly rang out was not the sound of a cannon, but the ominous roars of the chaos dragons.
They exhibited a momentum incomparable to that during the first onslaught or the Lickalten battle.
The monstrosity's power was amplifying the strength of the chaos dragons.
The chaos dragons pouring out from under Ram quickly surpassed a thousand.
Without a moment's rest, Ram continued to spew out chaos dragons and black lines.
This was not the welcoming ceremony Vera Din had anticipated.
'Send out chaos dragons and black lines instead of firing the main cannon?'
The battle showed a hard-to-understand flow from the start.
If such a large number of chaos dragons and black lines appear, the sky would naturally turn into a melee.
Even if it's a monstrosity, it wouldn't fire Ram's main cannon into a sky where friendly forces are mixed up.
'Is it to conserve the power used for the main cannon? Or do they think they can clean up after inducing a melee with that level of troops?'
Just as Vera Din had thought that far, an urgent report came from the watchtower.
"Leader! We have a report that the power of the spaceship Ram appears to have been cut off!"
"What did you say?"
"The movement of the main cannon, which had been protruding as the central part of Ram opened, has suddenly stopped. The chaos energy that was gathering to the main cannon has also dispersed!"

The power of Ram is the power of the monstrosity itself. If the power is cut off, it should mean that there's a problem with the monstrosity, and the chaos dragons and black lines should also not have been enhanced.
'The power of the monstrosity is intact, but only the link connected to the spaceship Ram is cut off...?'
Lyn Milcano.
The temporary alliance, excluding the Barmel Union, didn't know about her betrayal.
So they had no idea why Ram suddenly stopped.
"Leader, we don't know the cause, but this is an opportunity. We must break through as much as possible before Ram restarts."
Octavia said.
Vera Din thought the same. There was no reason to disagree. But an unexplainable unease was confusing his mind.
However, Vera Din soon decided to order a breakthrough. No solid reason to suppress his own unease came to mind.

"...Change all fleets to breakthrough formation. Among the three who were to be at the center of the main cannon defense, Fire Dragon Cadun and Knight Beil take the lead, and Orgal continues to prepare for defense."
As the fleet began to change formation, the monstrosity's airborne forces began to block their path.
"Gunnery positions. From now until the breakthrough is complete, autonomous firing will be permitted."
As soon as the order dropped, all fleets fired in unison. From the castle came the breath of chaos dragons and the fire of black lines.
The heavy noise without a break thundered in his ears, and the dizzying light of the clash of gunfire was engraved in his retina.
"I'll go out now, Leader."
"Good luck, Captain of the Specters."
Octavia went out onto the deck. Above the flagships of each fleet, the superhumans began to reveal themselves.

Hedo's Sword Dance, Dante's Formless Sword, Cirrus's Ice Barrier, Valkas's Black King Fist, Amela's War Weapon, Yulian's Thunder Bow Harumilla, Berakt and Bianca's Great Sword, Lanke's Rampage, Octavia's Light Magic and Specter's Chain Magic, etc.
All these techniques were slaughtering the incoming enemies.
The most prominent was Beil, who took the lead.
Every time his golden wings fluttered, hundreds of chaos dragons and black lines disintegrated into particles and disappeared somewhere.
In an aerial battle, Beil was like a disaster. His speed made interception impossible, and he was single-handedly responsible for the attack range of a fleet.
Ram's main cannon was still in a closed state. The chaos dragons and black lines continuously replenished from the bottom were not a significant threat.
From the beginning, a war of attrition had no meaning for the temporary alliance.
Unless a force capable of dispersing the power of the superhumans appeared, breaking through to the castle gate was just a matter of time.
However, about ten minutes later.
The temporary alliance had to face another unexpected situation.
"There's a purple reverse field forming up front!"
"The reverse field is pulling in the fleet...!"
It was a point where there was about 5 miles left to reach the monstrosity's castle.
The speed of the fleet began to accelerate faster than set due to the pull of the purple reverse field formed around the castle.
The monstrosity's airborne forces were not affected by this field at all.
While the fleet was slowing down, the enemy's counterattack followed.
Those on the deck were most affected by the reverse field.
Most of them could not fight properly as they set up their own shields, grabbed onto something, and resisted the pull.
The leading group of dragons were being pulled into the reversal field.
Beil used his golden power to pull some back from the reversal field, but it was impossible for him to prevent some from crashing into it.
[Roar!]
[Gasp...!]
The dragons that were caught in the reversal field let out a cry. As soon as they touched the reversal field, they started to crumble like a domino.
The situation of the fleet at the back being unable to easily escape from the opposite side of the reversal field continued.
'Fortunately, the reversal field is not invulnerable to physical attacks.'
When the fleet's bombardment hit the reversal field, cracks began to appear bit by bit.
'However, the speed at which the cracks are being repaired is too fast. If we try to break through with bombardment alone, it would take too much time.'
Ships started to sink one by one due to the chaos dragons and the dark lines, and Veradin carefully observed the situation.
The cracks caused by the attacks of individuals who had special powers like Beil were noticeably slower to recover than the ones from regular bombardment.
Therefore, Orugal and Beil, who were the key, had to destroy the reversal field, but the army of chaos also recognized that fact. They were persistently pressuring the two men.
"Change the position of Orugal and Kadun."
"We need some time, the chaos dragons have seized the rear!"
Orugal, who had been preparing for defense all the time, was dealing with them and holding on to the ships being pulled into the reversal field.
As Beil at the front was in the same situation, it was inevitable that it would take time to change the formation to center around the two and break the reversal field.
Then, one person who had been in Cojek's training room showed up for the first time.
"Veradin."
"I was about to call you."
Jin, the magic swordsman with the most special power.
"Did you finish meditating well?"
While the fleet was advancing towards the castle of the monstrosity, Jin was meditating alone in the training room for the last time.
It was a meditation to imagine the appearance of the sword that he had to exchange solely with Rosa and the monstrosity.
Jin stared at the castle of the monstrosity, which was faintly visible beyond the purple reversal field.
In the deepest part of that castle, Rosa must have been imagining a confrontation with him.
Jin slowly nodded his head.
Then, a flame formed on Veradin's staff. It was the 'Seal of Fire' that Keliac had used in the past in the Sword Emperor's War.
As Veradin began to swing his staff in the air, giant letters that glowed red were inscribed in the dark night sky.
Jin Lukandel is descending.
Like the opening of a gate, the front glass of Cojek was opened.
Jin, holding up the Bradamante soaked in his spirit, threw himself towards the battlefield.
